c: Motorola announces the MC6800 8-bit microprocessor.

t: Peddle and Mensch join MOS Technology
c: Engineers Chuck Peddle and Bill Mensch leave Motorola after completing work on the 6800 CPU and join MOS Technology.
The MITS Altair 8800, the first commercially successful hobby computer, is released.

t: Olivetti P6060 computer released with floppy drive
c: Olivetti released the personal computer Olivetti P6060, the first with an integrated floppy disk drive.

t: Gates and Allen implement BASIC for Altair
c: First microcomputer implementation of BASIC by Bill Gates and Paul Allen.
Norwegian company Mycron releases its MYCRO-1, the first single-board computer.

t: MOS Technology releases 6501 CPU, replaced by 6502
c: MOS Technology releases their 6501 CPU. which is pin-compatible with Motorola's 6800, who soon starts a lawsuit against them.

t: CSELT releases MUSA speech synthesis system
c: The laboratory CSELT released MUSA (MUltichannel Speaking Automaton), an early experiment of Speech Synthesis.
First laser printer introduced by IBM – the IBM 3800.
Introduction of the Intel 8085 chip.
Z80 chip released by Zilog.
MOS Technology introduces the KIM-1 microcomputer system as a demonstrator for its 6502 CPU.
Commodore buys MOS Technology in a stock trade.
Emacs text editing software created.
"5.25 inch floppy disks are introduced.
Commodore introduces the Commodore PET.

t: Commodore PET released in United Kingdom
c: Commodore PET released in the United Kingdom.

t: Activision founded by four Atari programmers
c: Four disgruntled Atari programmers leave and form Activision, the first third-party video game software publisher.
Texas Instruments releases the 16-bit TI-99/4 microcomputer.
Motorola releases the 68040 capable of 35 MIPS and integrated a far superior FPU.
Multimedia PC (MPC) Level 1 specification published by a council of companies including Microsoft and Creative Labs.

Borland acquires Ashton-Tate Corporation and the Dbase program.

c: The PowerPC 601, developed by IBM, Motorola and Apple Computer, was released.
The last "luggable" computer of the Compaq Portable series, the Compaq Portable 486, was released.
IBM ThinkPad 700C laptop created.
Commercial providers were allowed to sell Internet connections to individuals.
Release of the first version of ELOQUENS, a text-to-speech commercial software, from CSELT.

t: The Virtual Journal, first web magazine
c: The first web magazine, The Virtual Journal, is published but fails commercially.
The MP3 file format was published.
Several major PC games are released, such as Command & Conquer, Alone in the Dark 2, Theme Park, Magic Carpet, Descent and Little Big Adventure.
Peter Shor devises an algorithm which lets quantum computers determine the factorization of large integers quickly.
Motorola released the 68060 processor.
Adobe Photoshop 3.0 graphics editing software released.
Nokia released the Nokia 9000, the first of Nokia's smartphones.
2010 – Apple releases the iPhone 4.
2011 – Lenovo releases the first ThinkPad X1.
2011 – The first Chromebooks, by Acer and Samsung, go on sale.
2011 – The first 4 terabyte hard drive is released by Seagate.
2012 – Raspberry Pi, a bare-bones, low-cost credit-card sized computer created by volunteers mostly drawn from academia and the UK tech industry, is released…

2012 – September 11

September 11 is the 254th day of the year (255th in leap years) in the Gregorian calendar; 111 days remain until the end of the year.

t: Intel demonstrates Next Unit of Computing
c: 2012 – Intel demonstrates its Next Unit of Computing, a motherboard measuring only 4 × 4 in (10 × 10 cm).
2012 – TDK demonstrates a 2 terabyte hard drive on a single 3.5-inch platter.
2012 – Microsoft releases the operating system Windows 8.
2012 – Nintendo releases the Wii U in North America.

t: Apple releases Retina Display MacBook Pro
c: 2013 – Apple releases the first Retina Display MacBook Pro.

2013 – September 20

September 20 is the 263rd day of the year (264th in leap years) in the Gregorian calendar; 102 days remain until the end of the year.

t: Apple releases iPhone 5s with A7 chip
c: 2013 – Apple releases the iPhone 5s, powered by the Apple A7 SoC which the company proclaimed to be the first 64 bit processor to be used on a smartphone.
2013 – Sony releases the PlayStation 4 in the United States and in Europe 2 weeks later on November 29.
2013 – Microsoft releases Xbox One.
2014 – Introduction of the RISC-V architecture with its instruction set.
2014 – The first 8 terabyte hard drive is released by Seagate.
2014 – Google releases the 64-bit version of Chrome for Windows.
2014 – Intel unveiled its first eight-core desktop processor, the Intel Core i7-5960X.
2015 – Microsoft releases the operating system Windows 10.
2015 – AlphaGo was the first Go AI computer program developed by Google to defeat a professional human opponent on a full-sized board without handicap.
2016 – The High Bandwidth Memory 2 standard is released by JEDEC.
2016 – Fixstars Solutions releases the world's first 13 TB SSD.
2017 – Nintendo releases the hybrid gaming console Nintendo Switch.
2019 – Lexar announces the first SD card which can store 1 terabyte.

2019 – September 20

September 20 is the 263rd day of the year (264th in leap years) in the Gregorian calendar; 102 days remain until the end of the year.
2019 – Google claims to have achieved quantum supremacy.

t: João Gonçalves Zarco and Tristão Vaz Teixeira discover Porto Santo Island
c: 1418 – Portuguese explorers João Gonçalves Zarco and Tristão Vaz Teixeira discover Porto Santo Island in the Madeira archipelago.

c: 1431 – Diogo de Silves discovers the Azores.

t: Gil Eanes sails beyond Cape Bojador
c: 1434 – Gil Eanes passes Cabo de Não and becomes the first confirmed person to sail beyond Cape Bojador and return alive.

t: Dinis Dias reaches Senegal River mouth
c: 1444 – Dinis Dias reaches the mouth of the Senegal River.

t: Portuguese reach Cape Verde and Gambia River
c: 1446 – The Portuguese reach the mainland peninsula of Cape Verde and the Gambia River.

t: Alvise Cadamosto and Diogo Gomes discover Cape Verde Islands
c: 1456 – Alvise Cadamosto and Diogo Gomes discover the Cape Verde Islands, 560 kilometres (350 mi) west of the Cape Verde peninsula.

t: Pêro de Sintra reaches Sierra Leone
c: 1460 – Pêro de Sintra reaches Sierra Leone.
1470 – Cape Palmas is passed.

t: Fernão do Pó lands on island of Bioko
c: 1472 – Fernão do Pó lands on the island of Bioko.

t: Ruy de Sequeira discovers São Tomé and Príncipe
c: 1474–75 – Ruy de Sequeira discovers São Tomé and Príncipe.
1482 – Diogo Cão reaches the Congo River, where he erects a padrão ("pillar of stone").
1485–86 – Cão reaches Cape Cross, where he erects his last padrão.

c: 1499 – Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci explores the mouth of the Amazon River and reaches 6°S latitude, in present-day northern Brazil.
1499 – João Fernandes Lavrador, together with Pêro de Barcelos, sight Labrador.

t: Gaspar and Miguel Corte-Real reach and map Greenland
c: 1499 – Gaspar and Miguel Corte-Real reach and map Greenland.
